newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan press slams police over Bhutto killing.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan press slams police over Bhutto killing.

text.p: Pakistan newspapers condemned police on Sunday for killing Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto's estranged brother Murtaza and demanded an inquiry.

"There should be no cover-up and the guilty, regardless of their influence, should be punished," the English-language daily The Nation urged. "The Karachi police, a creation of the present government, has become a Frankenstein now. The monster needs to be de-fanged and brought under proper discipline."

It said it would be irresponsible to blame a grieving Benazir for the death of her only surviving brother, but added: "It is inevitable that some of the responsibility for this tragic outcome of the police action would devolve on her."
Murtaza, 42, leader of a breakaway faction of the ruling Pakistan People's Party (PPP), died in a shootout between his guards and police outside his Karachi home on Friday night.
The Karachi-based Dawn newspaper said police had been given a free hand in the past to quell militants of the city's Mohajir National Movement (MQM), but were now out of control.
"If there was a time when the foremost task in Karachi was to rein in the monster of terrorism unleashed by the MQM, the task is now wholly different," the paper said.
"It is to check the brutality and trigger-happiness of a police force which has imbibed one overriding lesson from its drive against the MQM: to shoot first and ask questions later."
The News said the killing would have serious political repercussions at a time when all was not well for Benazir.

"She will be most affected as inevitably the finger of guilt will be pointed at her, even though the accusation will be difficult to believe, as not only was Murtaza her brother, regardless of their political differences, but because he posed no threat to her," the English-language daily said.
"The government would do well to institute an immediate inquiry into the matter by a High Court judge to determine the facts behind the incident and identify the culprits."
It said Murtaza's death was a blow to the PPP, which it said was already in severe organisational disarray.

"Murtaza created splits in the PPP by taking on his sister, challenging her right to inherit the crown of leadership (their father) Zulfikar Ali Bhutto once wore and forging his own PPP-Shaheed Bhutto," the paper said.
Zulfikar Ali Bhutto was toppled in an army coup in 1977 and hanged two years later.
Nusrat Bhutto, mother of Benazir and Murtaza, could compound the PPP's agony if she aimed her anger and grief at her daughter, the newspaper added.

The Peshawar-based Frontier Post asked why police casualties in the fatal shootout had been so light. "The fact that there were seven fatalities on Murtaza's side whereas only two policemen received bullet wounds is rather intriguing," it said.
"It is also perplexing that if Murtaza's men were the first ones to open fire with their automatic guns, they should have inflicted higher casualties on the police force."
It said Murtaza had been hit six times in the upper body. "Clearly those who took aim at him wanted him dead."
